reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling's three facilities hold 44 MW of IT capacity, 2.7% of Virginia's announced 1,603 MW and 12th among the 25 state data centers that publish power figures.

That capacity translates to roughly 1,100 racks at 40 kW per rack, a meaningful but not dominant block of compute for AI training. The campus's 420,000 square feet and compliance certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, SOC 1 and 2, ISO 27001, and TIA-942 position it for regulated workloads, but the data does not show whether any of that power is actually allocated to AI.

The suitability score of 70 reflects published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing. Without tenant mix or utilization figures, the site's role in AI scaling remains unproven; it is a mid-tier power asset in a state where only 25 of 330 mapped facilities disclose capacity.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
